Estimate a nonparanormal Gaussian graphical model

Source: R/huge.R
huge_network.Rd

huge_network() estimates a nonparanormal Gaussian graphical model: a regularized partial-correlation network for variables that are normal only after an unknown monotone transformation. The nonparanormal model (Liu et al., 2009) relaxes the assumption of the Gaussian graphical model that the variables are jointly normal, an assumption that skewed or heavy-tailed questionnaire and symptom data often violate, so the network of partial correlations is defined on the transformed scale and is unaffected by the shape of each variable's distribution.

The transformation is estimated from the ranks of the observations. huge_network() transforms the data, computes the correlation matrix of the transformed variables and estimates a regularized partial-correlation network on it with the EBIC graphical lasso, as in ebic_glasso(). npn chooses the transformation: normal scores of the ranks with shrinkage (default) or truncation, or the "skeptic", a correlation derived from Spearman's rank correlation.

The returned network is the optimum of the penalized likelihood at the selected penalty, which certificate() checks.

For approximately normal data, ebic_glasso() fits the same model without the transformation; its cor_method = "auto" treats ordinal items through polychoric correlations instead. The model is the one fitted by huge::huge() with the nonparanormal transformation.

Usage

huge_network(
  data = NULL,
  cor_matrix = NULL,
  n = NULL,
  npn = c("shrinkage", "truncation", "skeptic"),
  gamma = 0.5,
  nlambda = 100L,
  lambda_min_ratio = 0.01,
  threshold = 0,
  na_method = c("pairwise", "listwise"),
  native = TRUE,
  labels = NULL
)

Arguments

data

A numeric data frame or matrix with one row per observation. Not needed when cor_matrix is given.

cor_matrix

A correlation matrix of already transformed data, used instead of data; no transformation is applied and n is required.

n

Sample size, required with cor_matrix: a single finite number= 1. Ignored when data is given.

npn

The transformation: "shrinkage" (default), "truncation" or "skeptic". Ignored with cor_matrix.

gamma

EBIC hyperparameter, a number >= 0; larger values favour sparser networks. Default 0.5.

nlambda

Number of penalties scanned, a whole number >= 2. Default 100.

lambda_min_ratio

Smallest penalty as a fraction of the largest, in (0, 1). Default 0.01.

threshold

Absolute partial correlation below which an edge is set to zero after estimation: a single number >= 0. Default 0. A logical value is refused. A positive value leaves the certificate missing.

na_method

Handling of missing values in data: "pairwise" (default) transforms each variable over its observed values and uses pairwise-complete correlations; "listwise" drops incomplete rows first.

native

TRUE (default) uses the package's own graphical lasso solver; FALSE uses the glasso package, which must be installed. See ebic_glasso().

labels

Optional node labels, one unique label per node of the network.

Value

A fitted network of class psychnet (psychnet) whose edge weights are partial correlations on the transformed scale. as.data.frame() returns one row per edge with columns from, to and weight; certificate() reports the check. The object also stores the precision matrix (precision), the selected penalty (lambda), gamma, the transformed correlation matrix (cor_matrix), the transformation used (npn, "precomputed" with cor_matrix) and the EBIC of the selected network (ebic).

Details

The shrinkage transform replaces each observation by \(\Phi^{-1}(r / (n + 1))\), with \(r\) its rank among the \(n\) observed values of the variable. The truncation transform uses \(\Phi^{-1}(r / n)\) truncated to \([\delta, 1 - \delta]\), with \(\delta = 1 / (4 n^{1/4} \sqrt{\pi \log n})\). The skeptic uses \(2 \sin(\pi \rho_S / 6)\), with \(\rho_S\) Spearman's correlation. A correlation matrix that is not positive definite (possible for the skeptic and for pairwise data) is adjusted to the nearest positive-definite matrix before estimation.

The penalty path, the EBIC and the certificate are those of ebic_glasso() with its default settings; the certificate is computed by glasso_kkt() on the transformed correlation matrix. After a positive threshold the certificate is missing; print() still shows the value for the network before thresholding.

Conditions

psychnet_bad_input when an argument is out of range, threshold is logical, cor_matrix is not a finite, symmetric, positive semi-definite matrix with a positive diagonal, n is missing with cor_matrix, data has fewer than two usable variables, a pair of variables is never observed together, labels do not match the nodes, or native = FALSE without the glasso package; psychnet_constant_variable (warning) when a constant or all-missing column is dropped.

References

Liu, H., Lafferty, J., & Wasserman, L. (2009). The nonparanormal: Semiparametric estimation of high dimensional undirected graphs. Journal of Machine Learning Research, 10, 2295-2328.

Foygel, R., & Drton, M. (2010). Extended Bayesian information criteria for Gaussian graphical models. Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems, 23, 604-612.

Friedman, J., Hastie, T., & Tibshirani, R. (2008). Sparse inverse covariance estimation with the graphical lasso. Biostatistics, 9(3), 432-441. doi:10.1093/biostatistics/kxm045

See also

ebic_glasso() for the untransformed model; certificate() and glasso_kkt() for the check; psychnet(), which routes method = "huge" here; psychnet for the result.

Examples

set.seed(1)
x <- matrix(stats::rnorm(300 * 5), 300, 5)
x <- exp(x %*% chol(0.4^abs(outer(1:5, 1:5, "-"))))   # break normality
huge_network(x)
#> <psychnet> huge network
#>   nodes: 5   edges: 5   (undirected)
#>   lambda: 0.06688   gamma: 0.5
#>   optimality (KKT residual): 5.30e-13
